Building basics and creative tools

A whole block is a 1 m cube. Hold Shift to work with half-metre pieces. In creative mode, the brushes build lines, walls, floors and copies in one action, and Ctrl+Z undoes your last building action.

Voxelgame main dd29d91 · 6 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides

Place a block

  1. Select a block in the hotbar with keys 1 to 0, or pick it from the Build catalog in creative.
  2. Aim at the face where you want the block. A ghost shows the cell it will fill.
  3. Right-click to place one block. The held item must be a block. With a bow, rifle or throwing rock in hand, right-click aims or throws instead.

A whole block is eight half-metre pieces. In survival, each whole block uses 8 pieces of that material from your pack, and the game says so if you are short. Creative placement is free. Placing blocks

Good to know. If any part of the target cell is occupied, the whole block is refused and the outline turns red. You cannot place a block inside yourself. Plants and water in the target cell are overwritten.

Picking, water and placement limits

In creative, middle-click the block you aim at to pick it. If the block is already in a hotbar slot, that slot is selected. Otherwise the block is held without changing your other slots. Aiming at a door picks the closed door. Middle-click does nothing in survival. Pick a block (middle click)

Your aim passes through water to the first solid block. Stand on the shore and aim at a lake or sea bed, then build up from it. You cannot click the water surface itself. Placed blocks replace water and plants in their cell. Building in and under water

A block is refused, with a message in the status line, when:

  • Only blocks can be placed. Tools, food and other items cannot.
  • Your hands are empty, or a tool, bow, rifle or throwing rock is in hand.
  • A solid block is in the target cell.
  • In survival, your pack does not have 8 pieces of the material for a whole block.
  • The world already holds 200,000 changed blocks. New building is refused, and the save warns before the limit. What cannot be placed or edited

Flowing water (creative)

The Water block in the creative catalog is a flowing source. Right-click with Water selected to place one. It spreads up to 7 half-metre cells sideways and pours down over edges. Flowing water does not go away on its own. Flowing water (placing and blocking water)

  • Placing a block into water replaces that water cell.
  • Digging next to the sea or a lake lets water flow into the new gap.
  • Survival players cannot pick up or place water. There are no buckets.
  • The other five water types are blocks. They do not flow.
Tip. To stop unwanted flowing water, fill each wet cell with blocks. On a multiplayer server the server runs the water.

Half-metre pieces

Hold Shift to work on one half-metre piece instead of a whole cube. Use it for half steps, thin walls, trim and carving. There are no slabs, stairs or sloped blocks; you build those shapes from pieces. Half-metre detail building (hold Shift) Target outline and placement ghost

Key or actionWhat it does
Shift + Right clickPlace one half-metre piece.
Shift + Left clickCarve one half-metre piece from a block. Logs and cactus still fell the whole tree or stem.
F1Clean view. Hides the outline, ghost and HUD while you play.
Careful. Holding Shift also sneaks on foot, dives in water and descends while flying.

Doors

Doors are built from boards. A small door is one metre wide and two metres tall, with one leaf. A wide door is two metres wide and three metres tall, with two one-metre leaves. Wooden doors

  • Wooden door: one block of boards. Craft it in the Timber section.
  • Wide wooden door: two blocks of boards.
  • Hold the door and right click solid ground to hang it. The spot needs free space and solid ground under it.
  • Right click a hung door to open it, and right click again to close it. A door swings away from the player who opens it, from either side.
  • A door will not open if anything other than air, water or plants is in its swing path. Clear the space and try again.
  • You cannot close a door while you stand in its opening. Step out first.
  • Hitting the door itself takes the whole door down. In survival it goes back into your pack if there is room; if the pack is full, it is left hanging. Mining a block next to an open leaf leaves the door standing.
Good to know. Doors cannot be hung or opened on a server yet. Blueprints skip door leaves, so a door is not copied.

Wooden chests

A wooden chest is one metre cube of storage. It keeps items where you set it down, so you can leave things at a build site. Wooden chests

  • Wooden chest: one block of boards. Craft it in the Timber section.
  • Hold the chest and right click to set it down. It fills the metre cell under the ghost, with the latch toward you.
  • Right click a chest within 6 m to open its Chest tab. Your pack and the chest sit side by side.
  • Click an item to move one across. Shift+click moves all of that item.
  • A chest holds up to 250 capacity and up to 64 kinds of item.
  • To take a chest up, break it. In survival it goes back into your pack with everything inside, but only if the pack has room for all of it. In creative, empty it first.
Good to know. Chests cannot be set down, opened or taken up on a server yet. Blasts, tracks, brushes, copy and blueprints leave chest cells alone.

Creative brushes

In creative mode, press B to move to the next brush. The order is Block, Line, Wall, Floor, Replace, Copy, Blueprint, Bench, Railing and Roof. You can also pick a brush from the E > Build tab. Creative brushes (B)

  • Block: Right-click to place one block.
  • Line: Right-click once to set the first corner, aim at the far end and right-click again. The line follows the longer direction. Line, Wall and Floor brushes
  • Wall: Same two clicks. The wall stands upright along the longer horizontal direction.
  • Floor: Same two clicks. The floor stays level at the height of the first corner.
  • Replace: Aim at a block of the material to swap and right-click. Aim at the opposite corner and right-click again. Matching blocks in the box become the block in your hand. Replace brush
  • Copy: Right-click two opposite corners to copy every block in that box except air and the Camp crate. Water and plants are copied too. Right-click again to paste at the ghost. R turns the paste 90 degrees. B discards the copy. Copy brush (copy and paste)
  • Blueprint: Save a build, then place it again. See the Blueprints section. Creative blueprints (save and place builds)
  • Bench, Railing, Roof: One right-click stamps a fixed shape at the ghost. Press R first to turn it 90 degrees. Bench, Railing and Roof patterns
Good to know. Every brush except Block shows a ghost first. One action changes at most 512 half-metre pieces (64 whole blocks). Blueprints have their own limits. If a cell holds a solid block, nothing is built. Water and plants do not block a build. Replace is the exception: it swaps only the material you aim at. Hold Shift on the first click for half-metre steps.

Pressing B clears a corner selection or a copied selection. Copies are lost when you change brush or leave the world.

Blueprints

A blueprint is a build you save and place again. In creative mode it is free to place. In survival, placing it uses pieces from your pack. Blueprints do not work on servers yet.

Save a blueprint (creative)

  1. Press B until the brush says Blueprint. You can also pick it in E > Build.
  2. Aim at a ground corner of the build and press Shift + right-click. The status says First corner set.
  3. Aim at the opposite ground corner and press Shift + right-click again. The blueprint saves everything built above the lower corner inside the box.
  4. Aim where you want it. The ghost shows the result. Right-click to build it. The whole build is one undo step, so Ctrl+Z removes it.

Build a blueprint in survival

  1. Press B to take the Blueprint tool out. Press B again to put it away. In survival it is the only build tool, so B is the only key you need.
  2. Aim where you want the build. The ghost turns red when you lack pieces.
  3. Check the list on screen. It shows each material as carried / needed.
  4. Right-click to build. The build is paid for in one go, or refused whole.

Each half-metre piece you change costs one piece of the item that block drops when mined. A whole block is 8 pieces. Dirt-type turf costs dirt. Voxels that already hold the right block cost nothing. If you lack any material, nothing is built or spent, and the status names the missing items.

Key or actionWhat it does
RTurn the ghost 90 degrees.
Page Up / Page DownLift the ghost 1 m up or down.
Left / Right arrowsChoose another saved blueprint.
Delete, twiceDelete the selected blueprint and its file.
Good to know. The save leaves out water, cells you carved out of the terrain and the Camp crate. The status line says how many. A blueprint can be up to 128 m along any side and you can keep up to 64. Placement is refused if it would build over blocks you placed yourself or the Camp crate, or on top of you. Step back and try again.

Saved blueprints are plain files with the `.blueprint` extension in a folder named `blueprints`. The game looks for that folder where it starts. Without it, blueprints last only until you leave the session.

Planned, not in the game. Sharing or importing blueprints and a survival materials list are not in this version. Saving a blueprint in survival is not checked in play yet. They are tracked in the feature ledger.

Undo and redo

Key or actionWhat it does
Ctrl+ZUndo the last building action.
Ctrl+Shift+ZRedo.
Undo and Redo buttonsThe same actions, in the E > Build tab.

Undo covers brush actions, single blocks placed and blocks or trees you mined in creative. Undo and redo building

Good to know. Undo is refused with "Undo blocked" if the cells changed since, if it would put a block inside you, or if it would pass the save's edit limit. Survival actions and explosions are not recorded. History is cleared when you leave the world.

The Build tab and palettes

The E > Build tab holds a searchable catalog of every item, the brush button, Undo and Redo, four preset palettes and a Save palette button. The Build tab is only offered in creative. Creative catalog (Build tab) Build tab and material palettes

  • Click an item to take one. Shift-click to take as many as fit in your pack.
  • Right-click an item to remove one you carry. Shift-right-click removes all of them.
  • Middle-click an item to star it.
  • Hover an item and press 1 to 0, or drag it onto a slot, to bind it to the hotbar.
  1. Click Timber, Masonry, Coastal or Garden to fill the ten quick slots with that set. Slot 1 is selected.
  2. Click Save palette to store your current ten slots.
  3. Shift-click Save palette to load them back.
Careful. A preset replaces all ten quick slots. Click Save palette first if you want to keep them.
